chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'When a man has a concubine under him and he frees her,' so he said, 'It is not permissible for her to marry until her waiting period (iddah) of three months has elapsed, and if her master dies, her waiting period is four months and ten days.'
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for an emancipated concubine in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific iddah of three months for a concubine upon emancipation, distinguishing it from the widow's iddah of four months and ten days triggered by the master's death. It highlights the juristic nuance in Shia fiqh where the nature of the relationship (ownership vs. marriage) dictates the waiting period, ensuring the woman's lineage is clear before she may remarry.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man happens to have a concubine under him, so he frees her’. So he said, ‘It is not correct for her that she married until she fulfills her waiting period of three months, and if her master has died from her, so her waiting period is four months and ten (days)’.
